algorithm.Title: Sunburn
Definition: Damage to the skin caused by too much sun exposure.
Usually resolves within about a week and can be managed independently at home, but severe cases can progress to heat exhaustion or heatstroke.

KeyPoints: Affected skin may feel hot, sore, or painful, and typically flakes or peels a few days after the sunburn occurs.
Fair skin usually reddens or turns pink; darker skin tones may show minimal colour change.
Getting sunburnt increases the risk of skin cancer.

FirstAid: Get out of the sun immediately.
Cool the skin using a cool shower, bath, or damp towels.
Apply aftersun cream or unperfumed moisturiser.
Take paracetamol or ibuprofen as directed if needed.
Avoid petroleum jelly, ice packs, scratching, removing peeling skin, or popping blisters.

questions.Question: Is there confusion, fainting, a very high temperature with no sweating, or a rapid heartbeat suggesting heatstroke rather than simple sunburn?
questions.Information: R/O: heatstroke. NHS.UK heat-exhaustion/heatstroke guidance lists confusion and lack of coordination, hot skin without sweating, fast heartbeat or breathing difficulty, seizures, or loss of consciousness as 999-emergency criteria; NHS.UK sunburn guidance notes severe sunburn can progress to heat exhaustion and heatstroke.

questions.Question: Is the skin blistered or swollen, is the temperature very high or does the caller feel hot, cold, or shivery, does the caller feel very tired, dizzy, or sick, is there a headache or muscle cramps, or is the patient a baby or young child?
questions.Information: NHS.UK sunburn guidance lists these as reasons to contact NHS 111 or request an urgent GP appointment.

questions.Question: Is this mild-to-moderate sunburn without blistering or the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes most sunburn as resolving within about a week with home care.

advice.Title: Emergency heat-illness precautions
Content: Move to a cool place, cool the skin, and arrange emergency transport immediately.
Call Back If: worsening confusion, loss of consciousness.

advice.Title: Urgent sunburn review
Content: Cool the skin, stay hydrated, and arrange same-day medical review, especially for blistering or a young child.
Call Back If: fever worsens, increasing dizziness.

advice.Title: Home care for sunburn
Content: Get out of the sun, cool the skin with a cool shower or damp towels, apply aftersun or unperfumed moisturiser, stay hydrated, and take paracetamol or ibuprofen as needed.
Avoid alcohol and further sun exposure.
Call Back If: blistering develops, or fever, dizziness, or feeling very unwell develops.

references: NHS.UK. "Heat exhaustion and heatstroke." https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/heat-exhaustion-heatstroke/ (page last reviewed 28 May 2026, next review 28 May 2029).
